To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vinblastine and vincristine inhibit the mitogenic response of human lymphocytes to PHA, A23187, and periodate.

vincristine and/or vinblastine inhibit lymphocyte transformation by PHA, periodate and A23187, and that the drugs do not affect lymphocyte viability at concentrations that inhibit lymphocyte transformation.
the Vinca Alkaloids block lymphocyte mitogenesis induced by lectin or nonlectin mitogens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the Vinca Alkaloids on the immune response.
the mechanism of action of the Vinca Alkaloids.
the effects of Vinca alkaloids on the lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vincristine and/or vinblastine inhibit the lymphocyte mitogenic response by interfering with a step in the cell cycle which is common to lectin- and non-lectin-induced lymphocyte transformation.
the Vinca Alkaloids block lymphocyte activation at the level of the cell membrane, possibly by impairing the formation of a membrane receptor complex.
the Vinca drugs are effective in inhibiting lymphocyte transformation in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Vinca Alkaloids block lymphocyte proliferation by inhibiting the cell cycle at the G2/M transition.
the Vinca compounds inhibit lymphocyte proliferation induced by mitogens of different chemical structure and mechanism of action.
the Vinca drugs block mitogenic stimulation of lymphocyte transformation at a point after mitogen-receptor interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Vinca Alkaloids are a class of chemicals that can block lymphocyte transformation, and that this blockage is not specific to lectin mitogens.
the Vinca Alkaloids are not only cytotoxic, but can also impair the immune system.
the inhibition of lymphocyte transformation is not due to a direct effect on the mitogenic stimulus but rather to a block in the lymphocyte activation process.
